title: Old Faithful intervals rose after 3.5-to-5-minute eruptions in selected 2007-2025 records
abstract: We tested whether a change in recorded eruption duration can account for longer intervals at Old Faithful. We used a fixed GeyserTimes archive. We compared 2007-2008 with 2024-2025 in three shared 30-second duration groups from 3.5 to less than 5 minutes. The sample has 3,157 early and 429 late eruption-interval pairs. The mean interval rose by 8.91 minutes. After both periods were set to the same duration-group mix, the rise was 8.18 minutes, with conditional 95% three-month block limits of 6.87 to 9.33. The duration mix term was 0.73 minutes. A webcam-only comparison of 2020-2021 with 2024-2025 gave a standardized rise of 4.10 minutes, with limits of 2.82 to 4.86. Month adjustment and a within-group duration term gave rises of 8.11 and 3.99 minutes. The tested duration mix thus does not account for most of the rise in these records. The test covers common long-duration groups, not all eruption modes. Changes in sources, selective duration reports, missed eruptions, only two years per period, and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The results do not identify a physical cause or prove a change in groundwater recharge. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure, and an audit are included. Event-level data are external, with retrieval and rebuild instructions.
